title: feat: add hosted FFmpeg MCP
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds a stateless FFmpeg MCP backed by short-lived Cloudflare Containers
- Routes it through the hosted MCP registry and Gen billing proxy
- Streams public HTTPS inputs and stores outputs through the Media service
- Makes FFmpeg selectable by prompt agents through the shared registry
- Adds Worker, Media, gateway, billing, and deployment coverage

gist.headline: The hive found FFmpeg
gist.blurb: FFmpeg now lives in the hosted MCP garden, ready for agents that need to trim, convert, remix, or otherwise persuade media into a new shape. Polli brought a tiny tool belt; the containers politely disappear when the work is done.
gist.summary: Added a stateless hosted FFmpeg MCP running in short-lived Cloudflare Containers, with public HTTPS input streaming, Media-service output storage, Gen billing-proxy routing, and shared-registry availability for prompt agents.
gist.impact: Prompt agents can now select the hosted FFmpeg tool to process media inputs and receive stored outputs without developers needing to operate an FFmpeg server themselves.
gist.visual_concept: Depict FFmpeg as a friendly retro media-workshop machine: film reels, audio waveforms, and image frames travel through a small container-like processing station and emerge as neatly packed media files. Polli, wearing a tiny mechanic tool belt and safety goggles, adjusts the machine while a CRT monitor robot eagerly watches the transformation; code-plants and flowers make the infrastructure feel like a maintained garden rather than a server rack.
gist.image_prompt: Cozy pixel art scene of Polli, the cute yellow-and-brown striped bee mascot with pink cheek blush, light blue wings, tiny mechanic tool belt and safety goggles, tuning a friendly retro FFmpeg media-workshop machine as film reels, audio waveforms, and image frames stream through short-lived little container pods into a glowing output box; a chunky CRT monitor robot watches with curious square eyes beside sprouting code-plants and flowers. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft lime green (#ecf874) and pastel gradient background, chunky retro sprites, warm lighting, lo-fi vibes like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike, subtle CRT glow, pixel-font text: "FFMPEG MCP", nostalgic but beautiful and emotionally warm.
